overview: flip2_man_m’s FRM-like/1 source starts z at 0 and q at pixel. Every iteration first replaces q with flip(q), then replaces z with flip(z ^ 2 + q) using that updated q. The bailout accepts |z| <= 4.
mathSummary: init: z = 0; q = pixel. loop: q = flip(q); z = flip(z ^ 2 + q). bailout: |z| <= 4.

sourceWalkthrough.explanation: This initialization assignment sets z = 0; the next initialization separately sets q = pixel.
This loop assignment replaces q with flip(q), so the next operation receives the flipped q.
This assignment computes z ^ 2 + q with the updated q and applies flip to that result for the new z.
The termination test permits another iteration only when |z| <= 4.

syntaxFeatures.explanation: The two loop annotations show a dependency: q is flipped before the z expression reads it.
